az_lost_bandana_wall.blurb: Lost Bandana Wall is the busiest roped crag on Little Granite Mountain, in the desert hills north of Scottsdale. It holds ten climbs, mostly traditional with a few bolted lines. Roughly half run from 5.6 to 5.8, one sits at 5.9, and three are steeper 5.11 pitches, so it suits newer leaders and groups looking for a relaxed day. The granite is slot and crack oriented. The wall looks south and soaks up heat, which makes winter days pleasant but early fall and late spring uncomfortable. A short, easy scramble leads on or off at the east end.
az_lost_bandana_wall.parking_note: Leave the car at the Granite Mountain trailhead lot reached from 136th Street, in the area set aside for horse trailers.
az_lost_bandana_wall.approach: Walk west to the Powerline Trail and follow it about 0.6 mile, then turn onto the Granite Mountain Trail for roughly 0.3 mile. Next take the Granite Mountain Loop Trail around the hill until a climbers' path leads up to the base. About 1.4 miles in total, with a short uphill push at the end.

az_driftwood_wall_the.blurb: The Driftwood Wall is a steep, technical cliff in the Oasis section of Granite Gardens, in the Granite Dells just north of Prescott. Of its ten routes, five are bolted sport lines, four are trad and one is a top rope. Every grade falls in the 5.11 to 5.12 range, with most at 5.11, making this a place for experienced climbers rather than beginners. The granite stands out for being unusually overhanging by Dells standards. It faces south to southwest, so expect plenty of sun. Climbing is mostly on bolts with occasional gear.
az_driftwood_wall_the.parking_note: Use the large dirt lot on Granite Gardens Drive, a dirt road branching east off Highway 89 just north of the High Rappel area.
az_driftwood_wall_the.approach: Cross Granite Creek on the wooden footbridge by the lot, walk roughly 100 yards, and turn onto the first path heading uphill on the left. The wall is directly in front of you.

az_southeast_face.blurb: The Southeast Face is one of three faces on Boulderland, a cluster of big boulders in the Granite Basin area outside Prescott. It has ten climbs, seven of them top-rope lines and three trad, spanning easy 5.4 up to a single 5.11. Bolts on top make rigging ropes simple, which keeps it popular with beginners, families and instructors, while the middle grades give intermediate climbers plenty to do. The boulders are old-school, compact and quick to lap. Climbers' paths wind around the base, so the faces are easy to walk between. Watch for snakes among the rocks.
az_southeast_face.parking_note: Leave the car at the Metate parking lot at the end of Granite Basin Road.
az_southeast_face.approach: Hike south on trail 353 until the boulders appear on your right, then follow any climbers' path to the face. Roughly ten minutes of easy walking.

az_nail_up_rock.blurb: Nail up Rock is a small bouldering zone inside the Main Boulders at Groom Creek, in the pines south of Prescott at roughly 6,000 feet. It holds ten problems and no roped climbs. Most fall between V0 and V2, with a handful of V2s forming the core, one V3 and a single standout at V7, so it works well for climbers warming up or building volume. The boulders sit among trees but catch plenty of warm sun, and the coarse, crimpy surface rewards tough skin. Elevation keeps it cooler than the desert lowlands in summer.
